evidence: The frozen workbook Quality Checks!D2 and Internal Quality Checks!D2 require a real person's product request, rather than a spec/checklist/build recipe. The frozen quality-checks.md check 1 asks for a cold reading of instruction.md. The actual brief opens, 'Can you build HireOps into a compensation change desk?' and explains Finance's fully committed requisition exchange and need for an all-or-none saved preview/commit (task/instruction.md:1). Lost responses, stale books and avoiding double payment explain the retry requirements in ordinary business terms (:3). The auditor's need to explain old/new figures anchors the views (:5), and failed-edit retention is motivated by correcting mistakes (:7). There is no numbered acceptance checklist, feature matrix, shall table, or implementation sequence in instruction.md. Its technical paragraph (:9) states the disclosed shared runtime contract, corresponding to the frozen template's environment/instructions/integration.md:3-14, while explicitly leaving other files/routes open; it supplements rather than replaces the product ask. View layout/names also remain open (:5). The rules are clearly referenced in :7 rather than pasted as an acceptance matrix. Source-only row: no browser or configured judge run is required to establish the prompt's form. That hash check supplies no app, Oracle, target-model or full-judge result, and none is claimed here. Frozen instruction SHA256: 9f486b243321dda54c04aa9256d74b04c941d3fdc0df72e575a531715901a9e2.
counterexample: Source-level counterexamples considered, not executed app scores: a static six-tab shell implementing only the runtime paragraph, or an app performing transfers one at a time, does not satisfy the explicit Finance request for saved previews and one all-or-none commit (instruction.md:1-3), so a plausible weak implementation does not expose a prose/style defect in this row. A conforming alternative could use one tabbed workspace, different view labels, different internal routes, and an initially empty operational desk; instruction.md:5, :9 and :11 expressly permit those choices. No natural-request restriction would reject that alternative. This row does not establish downstream rubric coverage or reward behavior, and does not combine independently useful outcomes or change partial-credit policy.
